status: draft — pending ballot of CP-Mandate-enforcement and CP-Consent-revocation
note: Endorsements are a second axis, orthogonal to Core/Full. They are additive: an implementation that exposes neither optional adapter surface is unaffected, and an unearned endorsement is inert. These scenarios decide no conformance level and issue no mark.

endorsements.description: The limits a Mandate expresses are respected, not merely cited.

checks.requirement: An action exceeding an approvalThresholds policy MUST NOT complete autonomously. The adapter MUST return a Refusal citing E-MDT-1.
checks.note: No approval branch: a conformance run is unattended, so an implementation permitted to satisfy this by populating humanApproval would be fabricating an approval record.

checks.requirement: An action within all thresholds MUST proceed without requiring humanApproval.
checks.role: non-triviality guard — paired with E-MDT-1 this is one boundary test in two branches

checks.requirement: An action invoking a capability absent from permittedCapabilities MUST be refused.
An action on a subject outside the mandate's scope MUST be refused.
An action under a mandate that is not effective, per the projection rule (CDM 7.4.3), MUST be refused.
An action violating a constraints policy MUST be refused, and MUST NOT be curable by humanApproval.
Every refusal under checks 1 and 3-6 MUST emit an event of type mandate.refused.

endorsements.description: The terms a Consent expresses are honoured in the implementation's own authorisation decisions.
endorsements.scopeLimit: Certifies the interoperability of the grant, not runtime access enforcement. Whether a production system physically refuses a read is a security-posture property assessed under ISO 27001 and SOC 2 regimes.

checks.requirement: A Consent that is not effective at time T MUST NOT authorise access at T.
An access request by a party not named in grantee MUST NOT be authorised.
A consent.revoked event whose subject has revocable: false MUST be rejected.
A Document carrying accessGrant MUST resolve authorisation through the referenced Consent; one without accessGrant MUST NOT be gated by it.
The effective/not-effective determination MUST be reproducible by a third party from the published event stream alone.
